messages:
EngOps Bot: announce: pilot Dedicated pool 'nebula-mex1' is live in MEX1 (Mexico City). Initial capacity: 10 Nebula-G instances. Pool tags: #dedicated #nebula #mex1 :globe_with_meridians:
Carlos M: quick context: Nebula-G is a power-efficient GPU SKU tuned for multilingual customer-facing models and low-latency embeddings. Nominal VRAM ~80GB logical via host NVCache. Expect ~12-22% cost/unit improvement for embedding-heavy workloads vs a100 baseline.
Nidhi P: is this available for reservations or burst only?
Jules C: launch mode is conservative: 30% reserved commit, 70% burst. We will open larger reservation windows after week 2 if telemetry looks stable.
Finance Bot: billing: new SKU 'dedicated.nebula' enabled. Metering: per-instance-minute. Intro promo: 4% migration credit for teams that route steady traffic within first 45 days and tag reservations with team=.
Carlos M: routing/fallback notes: default prefers nebula-mex1 for latam-preferred routes. Fallback chain: nebula-mex1-compat -> global-a100-fallback -> strict routing toggle available in Console.
Nidhi P: any model compatibility caveats? quantization?
Carlos M: supports 8-bit and our experimental 4-bit dynamic path. Default KV cache per-worker is 10GB; for heavy RAG use model_profile="nebula-large-kv". No runtime ABI changes expected. If you see numeric quality differences, open an eval with Optimize and reference 'nebula-mex1'.
Infra Oncall: ops note: Nebula burst instances are soft-preemptible during local maintenance windows. Reserved commits are non-preemptible. We'll publish the MEX1 maintenance calendar to #infra-maintenance by EOD.
Jules C: reservation CLI example:
```
redwood reserve --pool nebula-mex1 --count 3 --duration 60d --commit monthly --tags team=search latam-early
```
Nidhi P: what's the fairshare policy? I remember earlier pools had edge fairshare issues.
Carlos M: new fairshare policy for Nebula pools in LATAM: burst allocation is weighted by recent regional usage + team tag (team=). This should favor local customers during peak hours. It's a pilot; feedback welcome.
EngOps Bot: operational reminder: label reservations with `team=` so costs map to team dashboards and fairshare weight applies.
Infra Oncall: performance/regression guidance: if you see >8% error increase or >25% p95 tail latency regression after migration, tag @Infra Oncall and add the route id + p95/p50/tokens/sec. Include a short repro (request id or curl).
Nidhi P: any lessons we learned from past rollouts (e.g., network flake in May-2025)?
Carlos M: yes  we're using stricter health-check thresholds and staggered agent warmups to avoid global reconvergence storms. Also added an automatic short-circuit to avoid cascading retries across regions.
Jules C: rollout timeline: day 0 soft-open (this), day 4 expand burst to 30 instances if health signals are green, day 14 enable annual commit UI and fairshare telemetry dashboard.
Finance Bot: note: early adopters who migrate a production route and keep it for 30 days get the 4% migration credit applied automatically. Tag `latam-early` to qualify.
EngOps Bot: docs: https://intra.redwood.dev/dedicated/nebula-mex1 (internal). Pool ID: nebula-mex1-007. API model_profile options: nebula-default / nebula-large-kv.
Infra Oncall: health checks are running. Expect short warmup spikes in CPU/GPU metrics not affecting user-facing latency. Will post updates here if anything unexpected.
Carlos M: thanks all. Please test canaries and report numbers here. Escalate on >8% error or >25% p95 regression. :thumbsup:
